newsitem.title: USA: Rouge Steel to report Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Rouge Steel to report Q4 loss.

text.p: Rouge Steel Co said Friday it expects to report a loss in the fourth quarter as a result of a restructuring of its interest in Eveleth Mines, a recent blast furnace outage and other operating problems.

The combined effect of these issues will result in a fourth quarter operating loss most likely in the range of $20 to $25 per ton," Gary Latendresse, vice president and chief financial officer, said in a statement.
Rouge said it completed an agreement to restructure its ownership interest in Eveleth Mines, an iron ore taconite-producing operation in Eveleth, Minn.

Under the terms of the agreement, Eveleth Taconite Co, a subsidiary of Rouge, has assumed a 45 percent equity position in Eveleth Mines LLC, a newly formed Minnesota which will operate under the name EVTAC Mining.
Rouge said the remaining owners of EVTAC Mining will be Virginia Horn Taconite Co, a unit of AK Steel Holding Corp and Ontario Eveleth Co, a subsidiary of Stelco Inc.
Oglebay Norton Co has sold its interests in Eveleth Mines, and EVTAC Mining will assume full responsibility for the management of the operations, Rouge said.

Rouge said its expected fourth quarter loss is a result of one-time adjustments associated with Eveleth and an unplanned blast furnace outage in mid-November, the late arrival of purchased slabs and continued operating problems, which caused lower-than-anticipated fourth quarter shipments.
The company said this will be its second quarterly operating loss in its seven years as an independent company, and both losses have occurred during quarters with blast furnace relines.

"We have managed our way through this very difficult period with the singular objective of protecting our customers from production interruptions at their facilities," Carl Valdiserri, chairman and chief executive, said of the furnace outage.
"At this point, our operations have now stabilized, our order book remains very strong, and we are optimistic about 1997," he said.
